basics.name: Noah Burnette
basics.label: I make software for the manufacturing industry
basics.summary: I am a software engineer who helps digitally transform manufacturing around the world.

work.name: Intellic Integration
highlights: Led development of large-scale, distributed industrial applications using Ignition and Unified Namespace (UNS) architecture.
Applied domain-driven design (DDD) principles to model complex operational and business workflows.

Designed and implemented reusable developer infrastructure in Python and Java, including a custom Java-based Ignition module for concurrent data structures, a lightweight ORM, and an automated test discovery library.
Developed Python microservices to support client-specific operational requirements.
Built internal tooling in Go and Python to accelerate deployment workflows and improve engineering efficiency.
Applied test-driven development (TDD) practices and automated testing to improve code reliability and maintainability.
Designed and implemented CI/CD pipelines to automate deployments and reduce regression risk.
Mentored junior engineers through code reviews and architectural discussions, improving code quality and engineering standards.
Authored technical documentation to support stakeholder adoption and long-term system maintainability.
Delivered solutions across multiple industrial sectors, including food and beverage and battery manufacturing.

work.name: Sierra Nevada Brewing Co.
highlights: Developed warehouse and quality-related systems using Ignition.
Wrote and optimized SQL stored procedures and views for inventory and laboratory reporting.
Implemented backend functionality in Python for data processing and enforcement.
Developed operator-facing interfaces to streamline data entry processes.
work.location: Mills River, North Carolina, United States

work.name: Microtech Knives
highlights: Deployed and maintained Linux-based infrastructure supporting internal systems.
Built and maintained Docker images to standardize development and workstation environments.
Performed network traffic analysis to identify vulnerabilities and troubleshoot connectivity issues.
Configured and managed Meraki networking hardware, including firewalls, switches, and access points.

projects.name: Ignition Apache Camel
projects.description: Java module that runs Apache Camel routes inside Ignition 8.3.
highlights: Embedded Apache Camel in Ignition so developers can connect manufacturing data to external systems through YAML or Jython routes without deploying a separate integration service.
Built adapters for Ignition tags, scripts and messaging, bringing platform-specific operations into Camel's routing framework.
Designed reusable connection and certificate configuration with separate runtimes per integration, allowing shared settings without sharing live runtime objects.

projects.name: slowrm
highlights: Bridged SQLAlchemy's query compiler with Ignition's database APIs, enabling model-based persistence through existing Gateway database connections.
Implemented object identity tracking, change detection and transaction-scoped sessions to replace repetitive persistence code and roll back uncommitted work automatically.

projects.name: Ignition Package Maker
projects.description: A CLI for packaging Ignition script modules as Python packages.
highlights: Built a Python CLI that converts Ignition project scripts into distributable packages, enabling shared libraries to be versioned and installed with pip.
Preserved module import paths and package metadata across rebuilds, allowing developers to maintain scripts in Ignition while distributing them through standard Python tooling.

projects.name: Ignition Sift (VS Code Extension)
projects.description: Barebones, stub-driven auto-imports for Ignition scripting projects.
highlights: Built a VS Code extension that generates Python type stubs from Ignition scripts, making project APIs available to Pyright without changing the deployed code.
Translated Python 2 type comments into annotated signatures and indexed symbols for Quick Fix imports, reducing manual lookup of nested script paths.
